newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's PPB seeks to delay re-election in court.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's PPB seeks to delay re-election in court.

text.p: The Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB), seeking to delay the government's plan to approve re-election in January, will challenge the legality of an extraordinary session of Congress called to deal with the issue.

An aide to PPB president, Sen. Espiridiao Amin, said the party would file a suit with Brazil's highest court, the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF), that the month-long session which began on Monday is unconstitutional.
The problem lay with the fact that the session had been called first by the presidency and then again by the heads of the Senate and Chamber of Deputies, the aide said.

But only the latter session request included on its agenda a constitutional amendment allowing re-election. "You can't have two sessions at the same time so the second one cannot be valid," the aide said.

The PPB is the party of former Sao Paulo mayor Paulo Maluf, a strident critic of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's plan to run for a second term in 1998 and whose own presidential dream relies heavily on defeating the re-election amendment.

Experts in Brazilian constitutional law said Wednesday's move was unlikely to have the desired effect. Three academics interviewed by national CBN radio said the double convocation of an extraordinary session of Congress was constitutional.
A spokesman for the high court said it was currently in recess and its one member on emergency call might not even hear the case until after the session was over.
